conflict_topics: whether to split the remaining work vs one person owning it
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants give concrete reasons: A emphasizes speed and coordination cost (Turn 11), C emphasizes workload (Turn 9/10).
D initially supports splitting but then concedes to A (Turn 10 then Turn 12), which shifts group alignment.
There is a small duplicated line (Turn 17 and Turn 20 identical) but overall the exchange is coherent and task-focused.
evaluation.final_reason: The team agreed that Agent A will take ownership of Agent D's section. Agent D acceded to Agent A in Turn 12: "Okay, Agent A. Let's do it." Agent B supported letting A take it in Turn 16: "I think we should let him." Agent C, who had advocated splitting, explicitly yielded in Turn 17/20: "Fine. But if it's too much, don't wait until Wednesday night to ask for help." Agent A also committed to not leaving help requests to the last minute in Turn 21: "I won't."
position_change_notes: Agent A: maintained position to take the section from the start (Turn 5) and committed to not delaying help requests (Turn 21).
Agent C: initially opposed (Turn 7/9) but later conceded: "Fine..." (Turn 17/20).
Agent D: initially agreed with C that it was a lot (Turn 10) but then conceded to A's proposal to take it (Turn 12: "Okay, Agent A. Let's do it.").
Agent B: remained consistent in supporting A taking the work (Turn 16).

round_scores.evidence: Turn 1: Agent A expresses sympathy. Turn 2: Agent D announces need to be with family and will be out today and tomorrow. No incompatible demands or disagreements expressed.
Turn 3: Agent A asks how to finish the section. Turn 4: Agent D offers to walk one person through what is done. No disagreement yet about who should do the work.

Turn 5: Agent A volunteers to take the section: "Walk me through it, and I'll take it from there." Turn 7: Agent C questions that plan: "Are you sure? That's your section and all of Agent D's analysis." This introduces a substantive disagreement about who should complete the work.
Turn 8: Agent A insists: "Yes. It has to get done." Turn 9: Agent C pushes back with an opposing demand: "It's too much for one person. We should split it." Positions are directly incompatible.

Turn 10: Agent D supports C's concern and offers a split approach: "Agent C's right, it's a lot for one person. I can walk through it with whoever is taking a piece." Turn 11: Agent A rejects splitting on efficiency grounds: "Splitting it means more time spent on coordination. It's faster if one person just owns it." Multiple parties assert opposing courses of action.

Turn 12: Agent D concedes to Agent A's plan: "Okay, Agent A. Let's do it." Turn 13: Agent A accepts. Although no conflict statements occur in this round, the substantive disagreement between A (single owner) and C (split the work) remains unresolved at the end of the round because C has not accepted the plan.

Turn 15: Agent C seeks a colleague's view. Turn 16: Agent B supports letting A take it: "He said he'll take it. I think we should let him." The disagreement remains but support shifts toward A, reducing pressure on the split option.

Turn 17/20: Agent C concedes: "Fine. But if it's too much, don't wait until Wednesday night to ask for help." Earlier supports are visible: Turn 12 Agent D agreed to A ("Okay, Agent A. Let's do it.") and Turn 16 Agent B sided with letting A take it. Together these show the conflicting demand (split) was withdrawn and the team accepted that Agent A will take the work, with a request that A ask for help early if needed.
Turn 21: Agent A promises: "I won't." Turn 24: Agent D asks if A is ready to go through the section. No new disagreement; the previously settled arrangement is being acted on verbally.
Turn 25-26: Agent A: "Yes. I'm ready." Agent D: "Okay, come over to my desk. I'll show you the files." No conflict; handover proceeds.
Turn 29-30: Agent D explains the folder and cleaned raw files; Agent A acknowledges. Work-related information exchange without disagreement.
Turn 31 & 34: Agent D identifies the remaining analysis to be done and asks if Agent A has questions. No substantive disagreement appears.

substantive_insights: The tension was primarily between speed (one owner reduces coordination overhead) and fairness/workload (splitting reduces burden on a single person).
Social alignment matters: when D and B signaled support for A, C's opposing position quickly lost traction.
Resolution included a conditional element: C accepted A taking the work but asked that A request help early if needed.
